| Audience Type | Strategic frame | B2B / B2C / Hybrid (internal+external) | — |
| Handoff Readiness | Output usability for downstream teams | Internal clarity only / Designer-ready brief / Agency-ready full handoff package | Agency-ready requires Full Breadth |

**Invalid combinations the configurator must block:**
- Sprint pace + Deep depth
- Sprint pace + Slack support

You're describing **pure SaaS** — software with seat-based pricing and tiers already in place. SaaS is already modular by nature: features, seats, usage limits, and integrations are the atoms, and your tier structure (Free / Pro / Enterprise) is already the standard freemium → self-serve → sales-led ladder.

**Intelligent Clay** is for productizing **services** — consulting, coaching, agency work, done-for-you offerings — where human delivery time is the constraint and the work is currently too custom to scale. That's not your problem.

### What you likely actually want

Depending on which question is really driving this, redirect to:

- **Packaging/pricing strategy for SaaS** — feature gating across tiers, value-metric selection (per-seat vs. per-project vs. per-action), expansion revenue design. This is a SaaS pricing exercise, not a productization one.
- **PLG / self-serve motion design** — how Free converts to Pro, how Pro expands to Enterprise. A growth/PLG framework fits better.
- **Enterprise tier definition** — if "custom Enterprise" is the actual pain (every deal bespoke, sales cycles dragging), that's the one slice where service-style decomposition could help: onboarding, implementation, CSM access, and SLAs *are* service atoms bolted onto your SaaS.

**That last one is the only place I can help.** If your real question is *"my Enterprise tier is too custom — every deal is a snowflake, and I want to productize the human-delivered wrapper around the software,"* then yes — I can decompose the Enterprise services layer (onboarding, implementation, training, dedicated CSM, custom integrations, SLAs) into atoms, dimensions, and sub-tiers.

Handmade leather wallets are a **physical product**, not a service. There's nothing to atomize into time blocks, access tiers, or support levels — a wallet is a wallet. What you're looking for is **SKU and bundle logic**, not service productization.

**What you probably want instead:**

- **Variant architecture** — leather type (full-grain/bridle/exotic), thread color, card slot count, monogramming, edge finish. Each becomes a configurable variant on the product page.
- **Tiered SKUs** — Classic ($120), Signature (premium leather, +$80), Heirloom (exotic leather + monogram + gift box, +$200).
- **Bundle logic** — wallet + cardholder + keychain at a discount; "his & hers" sets; corporate gifting packs.
- **Build-your-own configurator** — Shopify apps like Zakeke, Kickflip, or Teeinblue let customers pick leather + thread + monogram with live price updates.

This is e-commerce merchandising, not service modularization. A Shopify-focused consultant or a product-line strategist would be the right help — or just a configurator app on your existing store.

**One exception worth flagging:** if you also offer *bespoke commissions* (custom-designed wallets with consultation, sketching, client approval rounds), *that* portion is a service and this skill would apply to it. If that's part of your business, tell me about the commission process and I'll run the blueprint on that piece.

## Part 2 — Configuration Architecture

| Dimension | What it controls | Levels | Dependencies |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Depth** | Sophistication of output (atoms found, dimensions invented, anchor precision) | Generic / Vertical-aware / Benchmarked-with-$-data | Benchmarked requires Vertical Pack loaded |
| **Breadth (Vertical Packs)** | Which industry-specific dimension libraries are loaded | None / 1 pack / All packs / Custom pack | Custom pack requires Team tier or above |
| **Memory** | Persistence and sharing of prior runs | None / Solo persistent / Team-shared / Org-wide | Team-shared requires Team seats; Org-wide requires SSO add-on |
| **Format (Output Channels)** | Where the blueprint lands | Markdown only / +JSON-YAML / +Direct-to-Typeform-Webflow-Stripe / +Proposal doc generator | Direct-to-tool requires API keys configured |
| **Support** | Human-in-the-loop assistance | Community / Async review / Office hours / 1:1 workshops | 1:1 requires scheduling integration |
| **Self-Iteration** | How the skill improves itself | Manual PRs / Weekly Action / Continuous w/ telemetry | Continuous requires opt-in telemetry |
| **Seats** | Who can use it | Solo / Team (≤10) / Org (unlimited + SSO) | Org unlocks white-label |
| **White-Label** | Brandability | Off / On (logo+name) / Full (own domain, hide attribution) | Full requires Org tier |

**Invalid combinations the configurator must block:**
- Benchmarked depth without at least one Vertical Pack loaded
- Team-shared memory on Solo seats
- White-label on Solo or Team tiers
- Direct-to-tool output without API credentials provided
- Continuous self-iteration without telemetry opt-in
- 1:1 workshops on Community support level (must upgrade Support)
- Custom vertical pack request on anything below Team

## Part 3 — Three Tiers + Build-Your-Own

| Tier | Configuration | Positioning | Pricing Logic |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Lite — Open Core** *(free, MIT)* | Depth: Generic · Breadth: None · Memory: None or Solo · Format: Markdown+JSON/YAML · Support: Community · Iteration: Manual/Weekly Action · Seats: Solo · White-label: Off | For solo consultants who want to productize their own offer once. Same skill as today — fully capable, fully free. | **$0.** Anchor: distribution + trust. The free tier *must* remain the load-bearing acquisition surface; never strip features that already shipped. |
| **Core — Practitioner** *(flagship)* | Depth: Vertical-aware · Breadth: 1 Vertical Pack (user's choice) · Memory: Solo persistent w/ managed claude-mem · Format: +Direct-to-Typeform/Webflow/Stripe · Support: Async review (48h) + weekly office hours · Iteration: Weekly Action managed · Seats: Solo · White-label: Off | For working consultants/coaches actively productizing client offers. You get the vertical pack for your niche, your blueprints export straight into your tools, and a human reviews your output. | **+$A/mo.** Anchor: less than one hour of the user's own consulting rate; replaces a $2–5K one-off productization engagement they'd otherwise buy. Flagship — the rational default. |
| **Premium — Studio** | Depth: Benchmarked w/ proprietary $ data · Breadth: All Vertical Packs + 1 custom pack · Memory: Team-shared · Format: All channels + proposal generator · Support: 1:1 workshops (quarterly) + dedicated async · Iteration: Continuous · Seats: Team (≤10) · White-label: On | For agencies and consulting firms productizing multiple service lines across a team. Shared memory means the firm's productization patterns compound. | **+$B/mo.** Anchor: below the cost of one mid-level strategist-week per quarter; replaces internal "ops/productization" hire. |

**Build-Your-Own framework**

- **Base price:** $0 (Lite is the floor)
- **Per-dimension upgrades (monthly):**
  - +1 Vertical Pack: `+$v`
  - Solo persistent memory: `+$m`
  - Team-shared memory: `+$m × 3`
  - Direct-to-tool exporters: `+$x`
  - Proposal generator: `+$x × 1.5`
  - Async review: `+$r`
  - Office hours: `+$r × 1.2`
  - 1:1 workshop (quarterly): `+$r × 4`
  - Continuous self-iteration: `+$i`
  - Team seats (per seat beyond solo): `+$s/seat`
  - White-label: `+$w` (Team), `+$w × 2` (Org/full)
  - Custom vertical pack (one-time): `+$C`
- **Floor:** $0 — Lite is always available standalone
- **Ceiling:** if BYO sum exceeds Premium price OR user requests >10 seats / SSO / full white-label → auto-route to **Org (custom quote)**
- **Configurator dependencies enforced:** all eight invalid combinations from Part 2

**Flagship-protection rule:** Core's bundle (1 vertical pack + solo memory + exporters + async + office hours + managed weekly iteration) summed à la carte must price **at least 30% above** the Core monthly price. Premium's bundle summed à la carte must price **at least 40% above** Premium. This keeps flagships the obviously-rational discount and BYO the path for users who genuinely only need one or two atoms.

**Critical structural note:** because the core skill is MIT and already public, the paywall cannot live in the skill code itself. The paid atoms must live in: (a) hosted services (managed memory, async review, exporters-as-API), (b) proprietary data (benchmark $ datasets, vertical packs released under a separate commercial license), and (c) human time (review, workshops). The MIT core stays free forever; productization happens *around* it, not *inside* it.
